findings.text: blocking: shutil.rmtree runs before record_removal, whose write/flush/fsync can fail even after opening the log succeeds; reclaim_unowned_scratch then returns only an error, so the tree is irreversibly removed without the required durable path/size/age/reason record; persist a removal intent before deletion and reconcile completion, with a successful-open/failing-write control.

blocking: one deadline created before both process scans is reused for every candidate's initial and final activity walk; if an early tree exhausts five seconds, every later candidate and every final recheck times out, and the next minute restarts the same sorted traversal, so readable stale unowned trees can survive forever; retain bounded progress or otherwise ensure fair eventual completion and test a slow first tree followed by a small eligible tree.
